newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's stock market at record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's stock market at record close.

text.p: Mexico's stock market closed at a record high of 3,974.42 points, a rise of 0.55 percent, or 21.80 points.
The stock market received a boost from positive sentiments over economic progress in Mexico, and the decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve on Tuesday to leave interest rates unchanged.

"Obviously the markets is responding to the news from yesterday and the Fed. Although it is a move upwards, there still isn't any euphoria," said Lars Schonander, director of analysis with Santander Invstment.
"We have a record, but I don't feel that the market is going move a lot from its actual levels. The market looks solid and we are in a favourable consolidation band," he said.
There were 117 active stocks, with 56 rising and 37 falling, with 24 remaining unchanged.
Mexican media group, Televisa led the charge, with its CPOs rising 8.30 pesos ($1.06) to close at 109 pesos ($13.87).
The share rose sharply after the company issued new information about a debt and corporate restructuring.
Among the weakest stocks were Sanmex B, which fell 9.21 percent, and Cofar B, which fell 8.78 percent.
